about: Grammar the tutor added on her Tutor page: her words, Claude's rewrite as a rule with a letter-number, and her answer. Only her 'Yes, add it' adds the rule (scripts/tutor_grammar.py).

items.text: كمان at the end. Don't worry about كمان.

versions.name: kamaan at the end = also
versions.one_line: To say 'also / too', put kamaan at the very end of the sentence, after the thing it adds to.

examples.english: This is my fiancée's favorite dish too.

examples.arabic: هذي الأكلة المفضلة عند خطيبتي كمان.
examples.english: This dish is my fiancée's favorite too.

versions.why: English puts 'also' near the verb; she moved kamaan to the end of the sentence for 'too'.

checked.why: No existing rule or proposal says kamaan goes at the end of the sentence to mean 'also'; P-FA-d28341e4 covers a different kamaan ('another', before the noun).

items.text: Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.

versions.name: ago = qabel + number + noun
versions.one_line: To say 'ago', put قبل in front of the number and time unit: قبل ثلاث سنين means three years ago.
versions.formula: qabel + number + plural time unit (qabel talat sneen)

examples.arabic: قبل كم يوم من السفرة بتحجز التذكرة؟
examples.english: How many days before the trip do you book the ticket?

versions.why: English puts 'ago' after the time phrase, but Arabic puts قبل in front of the number.

overlaps.name: number + noun
overlaps.why: Both use a number with a plural noun after it; this rule adds قبل in front of the whole phrase.

checked.why: No existing rule or proposal teaches 'ago' with قبل before a number and time unit; E1/E3 cover number+noun forms and the others are different uses of قبل.

items.text: يعني it's feminine but it sounds masculine or it's masculine

versions.name: hidden gender: nature words
versions.one_line: Some nature nouns look or sound masculine but are feminine (sun, fire, earth, sky), while هواء (air) is masculine even though it sounds feminine.
versions.formula: shams / nar / ard / sama = feminine; hawa = masculine

examples.english: So when does the sun rise?

versions.why: The gender of these nature nouns does not match their sound, so a learner cannot guess it from the word's shape.

overlaps.name: gender on adjectives
overlaps.why: A8 says a feminine noun takes a feminine adjective, but it assumes you already know which nouns are feminine; this rule supplies that for nature words.

checked.why: No existing rule or proposal covers hidden grammatical gender of nature nouns like sun, fire, sky; A8 and A10 only cover agreement, not which nouns are feminine.
